To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fat-storing multicolular cells expressing CCR 5 increase in the aging thyme and may be a component of the thyme stromal compartment, while adipocyte differentiation is influenced by CCR5 ligand expression in the aging thye.

1) the expression of chemokine receptors and chemokine ligands is increased in the thymes of aging mice; 2) the increased expression of CCR2, CCR5, CX3CR1, CXCR3, CCL3 and CCL5 was observed in the thymuses of aged mice; and 3) CCR5+ cells were found in the thymocytes, thymic stromas and adipocytes of aged mice.
fat-storing cells are increased in the thymes of old mice and that these cells express the chemokine receptor, CCR5, which is also increased in the thyme with aging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the fat-storing cell population in the aging thymi.
the role of CCR5 signaling in the differentiation and migration of adipocytes, and its potential involvement in the physiology of age-associated thymic adiposity.
the role of CCR5 in the physiology of adipocyte recruitment and differentiation within the aging microenvironment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the increased expression and distribution of fat-stores cells expressing CCRS in the aging thymi could be a result of increased CCL3, 4 and 5 ligands and the CCRS receptor in the thymuses of older mice.
the CCR5/CCR5 ligand system is likely to be involved in the regulation of the thymus microenvironment, including the recruitment and/or differentiation of preadipocytes.
the expression of chemokine receptors and chemokines may play a role on the adipocyte recruitment and differentiation in the thymocyte compartment of the aging thymic micro-environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CCL3, 4 and 5, which are increased in the aging thyme, may play a role on the differentiation of pre-adipocytes into fat-storing multilocalr cells.
the expression of the CCR5 chemokine receptor and its ligands may play a role during adipocyte differentiation and recruitment in the aging thyme.

CCL3, 4 and 5, which are expressed by thymic stromatal cells and thymocytes, may play a role as adipokines, regulating adipogenesis and migration of pre-adipocytes in the thymuses of aging individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased expression in CCR5 ligand expression in the aging thyme may be responsible for the increased presence of adipocytes in the thymis.

the increased expression and function of CCR5 ligand may contribute to the increased presence of adipocytes in the aging thyme and the increased expression of CCR3 may contribute to the adipocyte differentiation in vitro.
the expression of the CCR5 and CCL5 is increased in the aging thymi, which may play a role on adipocyte differentiation and migration within the thymus.
